steps.name: Bound Stop terminal contention
steps.description: Bound the concrete exit-observer/StopAllocation race so cleanup completes after at most two LWW proposals without fabricating lifecycle history or retaining process-local supervision.
criteria: After cleanup, StopAllocation attempts at most two fresh-read terminal proposals when the exit observer wins LWW contention.
A second rejected proposal returns success, releases supervision once, removes the driver route, emits no lifecycle occurrence, and preserves the competing row.
First acceptance, one rejection then acceptance, and an exact requested terminal retain their established occurrence and no-event outcomes.
Point-read and compound-write failures retain their existing typed errors and atomic no-partial-commit behavior.
steps.implementation_notes: Use the existing compound lifecycle write, supervision claim, driver route, and lifecycle bus. Preserve current typed errors and atomicity. Add no public or test-only production surface.

steps.name: Unwind post-assignment provision failure
steps.description: Use existing allocation-keyed teardown for every provision failure after slot assignment, releasing the slot only when structural cleanup succeeds and preserving established failure precedence.
criteria: Fresh start and same-id restart each attempt one allocation-keyed teardown after assigned network provisioning fails.
Successful teardown completes before slot release; the Failed row retains the original WorkloadNetnsProvisionFailed cause.
Failed teardown retains the slot and returns the existing cleanup error after a successful Failed write; a store failure keeps precedence.
Slot exhaustion before assignment invokes no teardown and retains its established failure disposition.
steps.implementation_notes: Reuse the existing structural teardown and error variants. Add no restart disposition, aggregate error, persistence, marker, scanner, boot-GC state, public API, or test-only production seam.

steps.name: Order same-id replacement teardown
steps.description: Make same-id replacement await prior driver, mTLS interception, and structural-network teardown before provisioning, identity work, or driver start for the replacement.
criteria: Same-id replacement starts provisioning only after prior driver stop, mTLS listener/rule/connection teardown, and structural-network teardown complete in order.
Driver NotFound proves absence; every other prior-stop error prevents mTLS, network, and replacement work.
A prior mTLS or structural teardown failure returns its existing typed error and prevents every replacement effect.
Successful structural teardown releases the old slot before replacement provisioning, identity work, and driver start.
Any post-assignment replacement provision failure obeys 02-08's teardown, slot-release, and error-precedence outcomes.
steps.implementation_notes: Use the existing awaited mTLS stop and structural teardown. Remove superseded restart-disposition behavior without adding a second cleanup protocol, public API, or test-only production seam.

steps.name: Activate BTR-3 lifecycle-port invariant
steps.description: Compose the accepted allocation-lifecycle port through production and socket-free simulation, then activate the fixed-seed BTR-3 same-ID restart invariant without changing worker internals or adding recovery machinery.
criteria: Production dispatchers await the accepted lifecycle port; the concrete worker remains sole owner, and existing start, stop, shutdown, gates, errors, and cleanup precedence persist.
The socket-free Sim adapter exposes exact Live/TeardownPending snapshots and ordered outcomes; one-shot stop faults retain ownership for retry and absent stop stays idempotent.
Same-ID restart observes driver stop, lifecycle stop, old-network teardown/slot release, replacement provision, identity, driver start, then lifecycle start, with no effect crossing a failed cut.
Seed 424242 registers and passes the canonical BTR-3 invariant across clean, transient lifecycle/network teardown, and replacement provision/identity/driver failure partitions within one retry.
The RED marker is removed; the checker fails when stop completion is missing/reordered or TeardownPending becomes absence, while real-worker integration evidence remains independent.
steps.implementation_notes: Implement only ADR-0089 section 7 and the feature delta's 2026-09-01 BTR-3 lifecycle-port amendment. Preserve ADR-0076's lower-level port and worker ordering. The Sim snapshot is observation-only; the invariant drives real dispatch and does not preload Live. Add no wrapper owner, socket, public inspection/probe/retry/cancellation surface, recovery protocol, generalized shutdown work, or second cleanup mechanism. File lists are guidance, not allowlists; tightly bounded caller/compiler fallout required by the accepted trait is in scope.
